text:
Agreed that kcat exclusions are whack-a-mole. The cause is that kcat is asked to do two jobs.

In the code its only job is to fix a gauge. In relative mode the loss cannot see a common factor on every steady-state rate constant (v is proportional to it), so the fitter rescales the result to make kcat equal scale_k_to_kcat. Any positive, finite quantity proportional to that factor fixes the gauge equally well. The saturating forward rate is a poor choice: for many valid mechanisms it is 0 (complete substrate inhibition), infinite (never saturates), dependent on how the substrates grow, ambiguous (PFK's ATP as substrate and regulator), or below the peak rate when abortive complexes or parallel routes exist.

Follow-up (agreed in chat, recorded as your choice): anchors at stated concentrations when the user has them, otherwise the peak turnover over all concentrations.
- Anchors: each is a measured turnover (kcat or specific activity) at stated concentrations of every substrate, product and regulator. Several anchors combine by geometric mean of measured/predicted, the log-space least-squares scale the fitter's loss already uses, and their spread is reported. Anchors stay out of the loss, so cross-validation is unaffected.
- No anchors: the scale makes the fitted mechanism's peak turnover over all concentrations equal 1. No data enter it.
- The peak is found by a deterministic multi-start search in log concentrations over a wide box (24 decades in the data's units), box corners included; no limit machinery. A saturating peak is underestimated by about 1e-12 relative.
- When the rate is still rising at the box edge (a law that never saturates) or is zero everywhere, the fit stays unscaled and is flagged; the scale never turns a fit into a failure.
- Replaces scale_k_to_kcat, _kcat_forward and the saturating-limit machinery. Absolute mode stays.

Peak search (verified): with no product present, the textbook random-order SS bi-bi never exceeds its rate with both substrates saturating; King's peaks are at fixed co-substrate. With a product present it can: when P leaves E(P) slowly, Q rebinds E(P) and the enzyme exits faster through E(Q) + P (125.6x the product-free saturated rate in a simple example). So "peak over all concentrations" can sit at an intermediate product concentration; whether the default peak should instead be taken with every product at zero (initial-rate conditions) is open for the spec.
